newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with NYMEX, low demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with NYMEX, low demand.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude values sagged early Monday as the entire energy complex fell on forecasts of milder temperatures for the East Coast, traders said.
West Coast traders seeking February shipments of Alaska North Slope (ANS) saw the 70-cent drop in NYMEX February crude helping nudge them into the market.
But others thought rainy forecasts for California would keep local demand weak despite the NYMEX sell-off.
"We're caught by more rain here, so there's no demand for the things we make," said a buyer who makes road asphalt.
ANS prices fell 45 cents to $24.07/24.27. The discount held at $1.53 under February West Texas Intermediate (WTI) following two deals January 8.
Buyers said recent poor weather off the West Coast raised concerns about slight shipping delays among traders, prompting several to buy last week.
Interest for Line 63 crude remained sluggish, with traders predicting that a lack shipping restrictions on Arco's Line 63 pipeline would keep supply ample.
"They weren't in the market of any (significant) type of volumes," said a trader who watches the grade's key buyer.
Crude traders at Texaco's Wilmington refinery were assessing if they needed to sell inventory following a early fire on one of the plant's gasoline-making units, players said.
"My understanding is they'll continue to run (January crude)," a trader said.
